query:
Two family members made essentially the same observation about Emeka needing rest after a demanding day — one grounding it in shared experience, the other in clinical reasoning. Who made the shared-experience framing, and what specifically distinguishes their message from the other person's?

Options:
A. Tolu
B. Auntie Grace
C. Adaeze
D. Uncle Dele
context:
[1] (about=Tolu, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:36:00) Clinically speaking, rest after exertion is appropriate. Just to note, Dad - if this is a pattern we should talk.
[2] (about=Seun, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:29:00) honestly Dad you should rest though I mean you were on your feet most of yesterday
[3] (about=Adaeze, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:27:00) The call happened. Your father was on for a little while. He said he needed to rest. God willing he is fine.
[4] (about=Auntie Grace, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:41:00) My dear Emeka, please listen to Tolu. I see too many patients who push through when they should be resting 🙏 a missed Sunday is fine, just rest
[5] (about=Emeka, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:18:00) Tired. E.
[6] (about=Funke, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T20:32:00) EMEKA 💀 said what he said 😂
[7] (about=Kayode, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:14:00) Thought he was tired from yesterday?
[8] (about=Nkem, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:23:00) I think it is quite natural after a full day like yesterday - I may be wrong but the drive back alone must have been tiring. Did the Sunday call happen this afternoon?
[9] (about=GROUP, said_by=Tolu, group-interaction, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Tolu notes Emeka missed church; group discusses it and concludes it was due to tiredness, not a pattern.
[10] (about=Uncle Dele, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:45:00) TOLU is correct that rest is appropriate. EMEKA has always been disciplined about his health. I am sure there is nothing to concern us. Regards, D.A.O.
agent_answer:
**B. Auntie Grace**

Auntie Grace made the shared-experience (experiential) framing. Her message grounds the need for rest in her own firsthand observation — *"I see too many patients who push through when they should be resting"* — and adds a personal, reassuring touch (*"a missed Sunday is fine, just rest"*).

This distinguishes her message from Tolu's, who framed the same point through **clinical reasoning**: *"Clinically speaking, rest after exertion is appropriate"* — adding a more diagnostic caution (*"if this is a pattern we should talk"*).
